title: incident-bot: integrate slo-toolkit auto-remediation suggestions and runbook quick-actions
author: Priya Sharma
description: Context: On-call runbooks for SLO-class incidents often require operators to triage and execute the same small remediation steps (restart worker, clear cache, adjust cache TTL, toggle a fallback routing policy). This PR integrates the slo-toolkit suggestion engine with incident-bot to surface vetted auto-remediation suggestions and to add runbook quick-action buttons that can be executed from the on-call Slack workflow or web UI. Motivation: reduce MTTD/MTTR by surfacing high-confidence, safety-checked actions and by making runbook steps executable with audit logs. What changed: 1) New suggestion pipeline that subscribes to slo-toolkit regression alerts and maps them to a curated action set with risk metadata (confidence, required role, expected impact). 2) Runbook quick-action framework in incident-bot core that presents actions as buttons in Slack messages and in the incident UI, with a confirmation flow, permission checks, and atomic execution via the runbook-executor service. 3) Safe mode and dry-run option: suggestions appear as proposals by default; teams can opt-in via a per-team config flag (incident-bot.team_config.allow_quick_actions=true) to enable exec. 4) Audit and telemetry: every suggested action and execution is logged to audit.logs and emits metrics (incident_bot.actions.suggested, .executed, .executed_failures) and tracing spans for correlated troubleshooting. 5) Rollout controls: feature gated behind "slo_auto_remediation_v1" feature flag, progressive rollout via feature-flags service (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and manual override per Linear project. Backwards compatibility: suggestions are additive and default to read-only proposals; no on-call workflow is forced to change. Security/Permissions: actions require RBAC checks; only team members with role 'oncall' or above and teams with allow_quick_actions allowed can execute. Design notes: we keep suggestion mapping curate-first: slo-toolkit returns candidate signals, operators create mapping entries in the runbook registry (yaml) which include validation hooks and rollback recipes. Testing: unit tests for mapping and permission checks, integration tests exercising a Slack action flow (mocked runbook-executor), e2e test simulating a SLO regression -> suggestion -> execute pipeline. CI: integration tests were flaky on first run (timing in sandbox), reran and all checks passed. Migration/ops: new DB table runbook_suggestions (lightweight indexed store) and new feature-flag booleans; migrations included. Operational playbook: if executions start failing due to runbook-executor timeouts, incident-bot falls back to showing the instruction-only runbook and emits an alert to SRE. Related: Linear ENG-4821 (slo-toolkit suggestion API), SRE-129 (oncall workflows), ENG-4990 (runbook-executor idempotency).

review_comments: Ethan Blake: Nice end-to-end. A few API nitpicks: prefer context-aware logging IDs in the suggestion handler and drop the global logger usage.
Priya Sharma: Thanks Ethan — switched to ctx-aware logger and added correlated trace IDs to suggestion messages.
Jordan Kim: Can we make the dry-run path the default for orgs with <5% traffic? Also please add an explicit timeout on runbook-executor calls to avoid blocking the request loop.
Priya Sharma: Implemented per-team default in team_config and added 3s executor timeout with retry logic (idempotent).
Sofia Mendes: Integration test looked fragile; added small retry/backoff and explicit cleanup for test fixtures. Approving after CI green.
Jordan Kim: Approved — small follow-ups for docs and a migration note requested before merge.
release_notes: Add slo-toolkit -> incident-bot suggestion integration and runbook quick-action framework. Feature gated (slo_auto_remediation_v1); default is proposal-only. Adds audit logging, telemetry, and RBAC checks. Rollout via feature flag. See docs/ops/auto_remediation_playbook.md for operational guidance.
